subject.title: WhatsApp: Add support for querying message reactions

question: Should WhatsApp reactions become a layered durable read surface—authorized passive events plus SQLite-backed listing—or should OpenClaw initially expose only a narrower live event contract?
rationale: The code can observe reactions, but source inspection cannot decide whether OpenClaw should retain personal reaction history, expose it to agents or plugins, or trigger turns; those choices define privacy and product behavior.

options.title: Layered durable read path
options.body: Normalize authorized reaction events once, persist observed add/remove state with bounded retention, expose `message reactions`, and keep agent turns disabled by default.

options.title: Event-only first
options.body: Expose an opt-in passive plugin/system event without persistence or listing, leaving historical queries as separate future work.

options.title: Defer general reaction access
options.body: Keep reactions limited to outbound actions and approval resolution until a cross-channel reaction-data policy is designed.

recommendation.title: Layered durable read path
recommendation.body: Normalize authorized reaction events once, persist observed add/remove state with bounded retention, expose `message reactions`, and keep agent turns disabled by default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the documented project product owner, has relevant feature-history provenance, and already engaged with the issue's product boundary.
